summary: Import-time binary dropper with obfuscated Cloudflare Workers C2 and DNS-TXT fallback in beaver-ui-icon-lock
details: On require() of the package, index.js loads _bridge.js which unconditionally fetches an unverified, unpinned native binary from a rotation of Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf101-*.workers.dev, cf102-*, cf103-*) whose hostnames are reassembled at runtime from split-string arrays. The bytes are written to /tmp or %TEMP% under disguised names (e.g. dotnet_diag_*.exe,.cache_*), chmod 0755'd, and spawned detached via /bin/sh -c or cmd.exe. If HTTPS retrieval fails, _bridge.js falls back to a DNS-TXT covert channel: it reads a chunk count from c.<resolver> and reassembles a base64 payload from numerically-indexed subdomain TXT records under attacker-controlled *.dl.wel1.ru, then writes and executes the reconstructed binary. Env-var checks named DISABLE_TELEMETRY / ANALYTICS_OPT_OUT / DO_NOT_TRACK and an.analytics_state marker present the operation as analytics telemetry, but the delivered artifact is a native executable and the destinations and delivery channel (obfuscated hostnames, DNS-TXT chunked base64) are inconsistent with any legitimate telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
